articles.title: Recover a lost queue notification with a SQLite outbox
articles.excerpt: A worker pops a notification, then stops before committing its work. If the queue is only a dispatch accelerator, recovery must start from a durable record. This runnable example stores three jobs in…
articles.body: A worker pops a notification, then stops before committing its work. If the queue is only a dispatch accelerator, recovery must start from a durable record. This runnable example stores three jobs in SQLite, removes one Spedo notification to simulate a crash, redispatches pending rows, and deliberately adds a duplicate. Four deliveries produce three local effects. The effect and processed-state transition share a single SQLite transaction. Run the failure case Requirements: Docker, Python 3, a free local port 6380. Save the full example below as transient_idempotent_job_accelerator.py .
articles.author: Dany Cohen

articles.title: My agent's memory contradicted itself and nobody noticed. I built a read-only audit CLI.
articles.excerpt: My agent's memory contradicted itself and nobody noticed. I built a read-only audit CLI. Last week I asked a simple question about an agent's memory: at one point in February, what did it believe the…
articles.body: My agent's memory contradicted itself and nobody noticed. I built a read-only audit CLI. Last week I asked a simple question about an agent's memory: at one point in February, what did it believe the database engine was? The answer came back with two values at once. Postgres 15 and Postgres 16. Both marked current. Both believed. The agent had not reasoned badly. Its memory was rotten, and nothing in the loop ever checked the store itself. A limit changes and both values stay current. An upgrade supersedes a fact that is never marked superseded. A TTL expires and nobody notices. A fact arrives with no record of where it came from. The agent then acts on stale or contradictory memory with full confidence, and the failure looks like a reasoning bug when it is really a data bug.

articles.title: AWS Emulators Are Useful, but They Are Not AWS
articles.excerpt: A local AWS emulator can make cloud development faster and safer. It can also create a false sense of confidence if you expect it to behave exactly like AWS. The useful question is not whether an emul…
articles.body: A local AWS emulator can make cloud development faster and safer. It can also create a false sense of confidence if you expect it to behave exactly like AWS. The useful question is not whether an emulator is "accurate." It is which parts of your application it can test well, and which risks still need a real AWS account. What an AWS emulator does An AWS emulator runs a local service endpoint that accepts AWS-style API requests. Your AWS CLI, SDK, or infrastructure tool can send requests to that endpoint instead of AWS. For example, the AWS CLI supports an endpoint override for a single command: aws s3 ls --endpoint-url http://localhost:4566 The command uses the local service only if something is listening at that endpoint.

articles.body: Disclosure: I work on nRouter. This post was drafted with AI assistance and reviewed by me before publishing. Every SDK guide is, underneath, a promise that the raw HTTP is sane. The fastest way to check that promise is to skip the SDK entirely. nRouter's cURL examples page is the one I send people who want to see the contract before they commit to a client library — here's what it actually shows. The whole setup is one export export NROUTER_API_KEY = "sk-nrouter-xxxxxxxxxxxx" curl https://api.nrouter.ai/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $NROUTER_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "openai/gpt-4o-mini", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"} ] }' That's the integration.

articles.body: TL;DR. "RLS Disabled in Public" (lint 0013_rls_disabled_in_public , level ERROR) means a table in an exposed schema has row level security off while anon or authenticated can select from it. In my local test the public key read all 3 of 3 rows from such a table and inserted a new one with 201 Created . Enable RLS, add a policy per operation and check the grants, all in one migration. I built a free Supabase security checker and this is the finding I see most in apps built with AI tools. Supabase's Security Advisor reports it as an error. Here is what it means and what it allowed when I reproduced it. What does "RLS disabled in public" mean? The Security Advisor runs a lint called rls_disabled_in_public .

articles.title: Strangle, don't rewrite: patterns around a COBOL core to modern Java
articles.excerpt: Say your bank runs its ledger on a COBOL core, and the mobile team wants a modern account inquiry API. Nobody wants a big-bang rewrite of the core, so someone draws a facade in front of the mainframe…
articles.body: Say your bank runs its ledger on a COBOL core, and the mobile team wants a modern account inquiry API. Nobody wants a big-bang rewrite of the core, so someone draws a facade in front of the mainframe and says the magic words: Strangler Fig. Route one operation at a time to new code, and let the old system shrink. That's the right starting point, and Martin Fowler's Strangler Fig Application page explains it well. The trouble starts the day after the facade goes in. The new service has to read packed decimals out of copybook records. It has to know whether a balance is posted or only memo-posted. It has to prove it computes the same interest as the old code before anyone flips a route. And once it publishes events, it has to survive the broker delivering the same event twice.

articles.title: Building an End-to-End News Video Pipeline with Python, Groq, and FFmpeg
articles.excerpt: Producing short-form news updates for platforms like YouTube Shorts is a repetitive task. The process almost always follows the exact same sequence: take a raw news headline, expand it into a timed br…
articles.body: Producing short-form news updates for platforms like YouTube Shorts is a repetitive task. The process almost always follows the exact same sequence: take a raw news headline, expand it into a timed broadcast script, generate an anchor video, transcribe the speech, burn dynamic subtitles, composite news graphics and audio, and upload the final cut with optimized titles and tags. Doing this manually takes anywhere from fifteen to thirty minutes per video clip. Even when using modern web tools for script generation and avatar synthesis, you end up acting as human middleware.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 13 – NGC… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. NGC 206 and the Star Clouds of Andromeda Explanation: The large stellar association cataloged as NGC 206 is nestled within the dusty arms of the neighboring Andromeda galaxy along with the galaxy’s pinkish star-forming regions. Also known as M31, the spiral galaxy is a mere 2.5 million light-years away. NGC 206 is found at the center of this sharp and detailed close-up of the southwestern extent of Andromeda’s disk.
